check: settle whether the two renamed arch-preparation cases count as never-run, which reverses part of last round's correction
theQuestion: Last round I corrected the never-run count from 23 to 21 on the grounds that two cases were renames rather than additions. That is only right if a rename leaves the test unchanged. Commit b90f5fc's message says it changed how the failure is injected, so the current bodies may never have run either.
whatTheDiffShows: The bodies did change. The old case called fixture(helper, FROZEN); the new one calls fixtureWithFailingDurable(helper, FROZEN). The class comment explains why: failure is now injected through the durable plan reader rather than through plan-schema construction, because the earlier fabrication - a write plan with an empty recipe hash - was itself the defect that 31a8530 removed.

soTheHonestDecomposition.note: 106 plus 2 plus 21 is 129. The two renamed cases are a distinct category: their names appeared in the old results, but not in their current form.

aClaimThatLookedLikeAContradiction.theCommitSays: These two GameTests had been failing since 31a8530 rewrote WallArchBackfill.
aClaimThatLookedLikeAContradiction.theResultsShow: The 10-03 results contain both old names with zero failures recorded anywhere in the file.
aClaimThatLookedLikeAContradiction.resolution: 31a8530 is dated 2026-10-06, two days after the 10-03 run. So they passed at that run and broke when the rewrite landed - the commit message describes a later state, not a contradiction.

whatThisMeansForThePendingRun: The results check should expect 129 cases and specifically confirm WallArchPreparationGameTests contributes four, of which three have never run in their current form - two renamed and re-bodied, one new.
correctionOfMyCorrection: Last round's 21 is not wrong as a count of tests never executed under any name, but it understates what has never run in its present form, which is 23. The closing procedure should carry both figures with their distinct meanings rather than one of them.
